description: Issue #830: swaps DeletedFile's fp.DeleteFileTenantScoped(...) call back to the non-tenant-scoped fp.DeleteFile(...) overload -- a compile-preserving method-name swap (both overloads exist on WtmFileProvider; DeleteFile is marked [Obsolete] as of this same PR, which this mutant patch also exercises does not fail the build). Checked against FileApiControllerHardeningTests830.DeletedFile_CrossTenant_DoesNotDeleteOtherTenantsFile_SameTenantDeleteSucceeds, which seeds two tenants with EnableTenant=true (mirroring MultiTenantSeedFixtureTests), logs in as tenant A's user, and asserts tenant B's FileAttachment row still physically exists (a real database read-back with ignoreQueryFilters:true) after tenant A's caller POSTs DeletedFile for tenant B's id. The controller always returns 200 either way (WtmFileProvider.DeleteFileCore treats a miss as a silent no-op), so the status code is asserted separately and is NOT what detects this mutant -- the read-back is.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.FileApiControll: tenant B's FileAttachment must still physically exist after tenant A's caller attempted to delete it by GUID

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first) with the mutant patch applied: "Assert.IsNotNull failed. #830: tenant B's FileAttachment must still physically exist after tenant A's caller attempted to delete it by GUID — DeleteFileTenantScoped must have resolved it via a tenant-A-scoped query (which cannot see tenant B's row) and found nothing to delete."
